ops.title: bundled.build()'s re-read trades a forever-eviction for an undetectable false-ready
ops.body:
Recorded 2026-08-01. The trade is deliberate and correct; this note exists so the residual is not
rediscovered as a surprise.

Phase 4 gave daemonkit's two Program placement policies different drift semantics. `copied`
(`Stable()`) freezes the build digest at construction; `bundled` (`InBundle()`) re-reads.

Why bundled must re-read: with a frozen digest, an `.app` upgraded under a long-lived Client made
`want` permanently stale, so every Ensure computed build != want, evicted a HEALTHY daemon, applied,
failed with "daemon came up as build X, want Y", and repeated forever. Proven red. The two largest
consumers (fusekit, cc-pool) are both InBundle.

The residual the re-read creates: launchd restarts a bundled daemon at the instant an installer
replaces `<app>/Contents/MacOS/<exe>`. The new process execs B1 (image already mapped) but
`buildDigest()` runs microseconds later and reads B2 off the path, so it publishes and records B2
while executing B1. `bundled.build()` also re-reads B2, so `decide(observed B2, want B2)` returns
ActionNothing and Ensure reports converged on a build the running process does not execute. **It
never self-corrects.** Under the frozen digest this same interleaving produced a loud (permanently
failing) error — so the re-read removes the only signal that would have flagged it.

`copied` has a mitigation for the same hazard: `replaced=true` forces an eviction. `bundled` cannot
have one — daemonkit does not deploy those bytes.

The only real fix is to stop measuring identity by re-reading a mutable path: digest the running
image's cdhash through `internal/trust`'s existing csops read, which no rename can move. That is its
own lane; a TODO at serve.go names it. See [[csops-audittoken-reads-a-suspended-child]] for the
measurement that the csops machinery works against another process.
